thesis: Tonight's close carries a risk premium for two inflation prints, not one. When CPI and PPI land on consecutive sessions the market prices the pair as a single block, and the duration holder gets paid to sit through the second, lower-information half of it: the PPI session pays TLT +25.8 bps when a CPI printed on its eve against +8.4 bps when one did not, and the session immediately before the print pays nothing at all. The other side is whoever bought protection across the block and unwinds it once the headline number is out, plus the rates shorts positioned for a producer print that almost never moves the story after CPI has. Consensus treats PPI as a footnote, which is the reason the premium survives to be collected. 95% of the payoff arrives in the 08:30 gap, so this is a one-session release trade and nothing else.

SPY's overnight legs sum to +10.76 bps across the five post-opex nights against 45 bps of MOC-to-MOO cost, which is 0.24x against a 5x bar, and the true anchor ranks 10 of 16 and 11 of 16 in its own offset placebo ladder. Against a trading-day-matched non-opex placebo SPY's overnight excess is positive at every horizon while IWM's is negative at every horizon and IWM's INTRADAY leg carries the sign instead. The dealer-hedging mechanism is also unmeasurable in this repo: option_surface_history holds 1 row and option_positioning_history 90, all dated 2026-08-05.

Eleven candidates over five axes and nine asset classes, twenty-eight check scripts, and nothing reached the bar. Three came close enough to be worth writing down, and each died to a different test. The morning had two genuinely unexamined surfaces and both came back empty: the opex anchor crossed with every non-equity class (gold, silver, duration, credit, energy, the dollar and China, a hundred cells whose excess standard deviation is 0.132pp with not one cell clearing a percentage point), and Jackson Hole on the two classes its five-class sweep never reached. That JH work turned up the structural fact that decides both: the August opex close IS the JH-5 anchor in 21 of 26 years, so the two lanes were one anchor family wearing two labels, and both labels were already closed. Of the twenty-one live watchlist entries, one fired all of its stated conditions for the first time and still died, on a trend-state rung the entry never encoded. The tape offered no shortage of extremes to work with, but today's specific readings sat on the wrong side of the cells that pay: gold thrusting from sixteen percent below its high rather than near it, silver deeper in drawdown than any historical anchor, energy at a fifty-two week high where the parked crude entry's own condition forbids the trade, and a midterm year that inverts the one index cell with a strong parent.
